title: When the Passage Sings
premise: Ines Joubert has spent a decade drifting between dig sites, outrunning the memory of the father whose methods she inherited and whose name she refuses to speak. When rival archaeologist Marguerite Voss hires Ines's crew to excavate a river cave in the Mekong delta—the same site her father swore off after a fatal collapse—Ines discovers Voss is chasing proof that would vindicate her father's discredited theories, and that the permits expire with the monsoon. Trapped on a leaking boat with a local guide who knew her father, Ines must choose between exposing the truth of what really happened in that cave and protecting the loyalty of the crew who've become her only family. She chooses truth: the collapse was her father's cover for saving his workers' lives, and publishing it costs her the anonymity she hid behind but finally gives her somewhere to stand.
about_author: Gideon Coldharbour is the pen name of a former river freight broker who spent seven years running cargo up the Mekong tributaries before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people who are better at leaving than staying.

chapters.title: The Weight of Staying
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Her crew finishes a profitable but unremarkable dig in Cambodia when Marguerite Voss arrives with permits for the Nam Kham cave—the site Ines's father abandoned twenty years ago after a collapse killed his mentor. Ines wants to refuse; her crew, broke and loyal to her, waits for her call. The beat is dread disguised as pragmatism as she signs on, telling herself it's just money.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, shifting to shared narration aboard the boat. The monsoon arrives early; the hull starts taking water, and their guide, Sophea, reveals he was a teenage laborer on her father's last expedition—and that her father ordered everyone out minutes before the collapse, then took the blame for shoddy surveying. Rising tension: Ines realizes the site isn't just dangerous geology; it's a buried lie she's been carrying.

chapters.title: Concession
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating Ines and crew POV. With hours left on the permits and the boat half-flooded, they reach the cave and find evidence confirming both the discovery and her father's heroism—but Voss arrives intending to publish only the find, keeping the old scandal alive to settle her own grudge. Ines must choose: seize credit quietly or fight Voss publicly while the river rises. She chooses the fight, nearly losing the crew's trust to win the truth.

chapters.title: A Place to Stand
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The flood forces them out with what they can carry, but Sophea's testimony and recovered field notes let Ines publish the full account, clearing her father's name at the cost of her own invisibility. Voss concedes with grudging respect. The crew stays—not because Ines stopped moving, but because she finally stopped running. The beat is quiet belonging earned through hard truth.
